title: Stephen Saad and Africa's First Generic ARV, Port Elizabeth, 2003
conflicts: The 2001 GSK licence's 30 per cent: Down To Earth says 30 per cent of net profit to NGOs with no royalty; other accounts (blocked) say net sales or a licensing fee; the story attributes the Down To Earth version to 'one report at the time'. FDA: Business Report dates FDA approval of the Port Elizabeth plant to December 2004, while the Mail & Guardian and Health-e date approval of the ARVs to January 2005; the story uses January 2005 and the narrower 'first generic maker cleared to supply under PEPFAR'. A single-source cost-fall figure (R95,000 to R1,200 a year) was left out.
notes: No substantial interview with Saad about the decision could be loaded (BusinessTech profile 403, Mandela University citation timed out, IRIN and aidsmap 403), so his voice comes from the 2003 press release and a 2001 report; the story leans on documented terms and outcomes. The episode is told as the 2001 licence leading to the August 2003 launch, with the Competition Commission case and 2005 FDA clearance as aftermath. Stance 'complicates': James's 'more inclusive side' set against activists whose refusal to settle widened the licences.
